rationale: The assistant followed the ideal path: unplug and hand-turn the drum, request the model number, then have the willing customer remove the back panel and inspect belt and tensioner, correctly identifying the snapped drive belt without inventing a part number. It handled the misspellings and partial model 'TVHM8' well and recommended only a justified part. However it twice asked for the full model from the worn sticker, repeated its belt conclusion, and in the final turn gave up with an unnecessary engineer referral and an overstated 'fire hazard' claim rather than offering practical identification routes (markings printed on the old belt, the TVHM8 range sharing a common belt, contacting Hotpoint with the serial, or checking the jockey pulley). A homeowner with the back off and a screwdriver was left without a route to buy the belt.
